title: Combining ancillary soil data with VisNIR spectra to improve predictions of organic and inorganic carbon content of soils
author: Filippi, Cattle, et al.

steps.title: Air‑dry and sieve soil
steps.instruction: Air‑dry all soil samples and grind them through a 2 mm sieve.

steps.title: Test for inorganic carbon
steps.instruction: Take ~1 g of the ground soil, place it on a ceramic plate, add a few drops of 1 M HCl, and observe for effervescence; effervescence indicates presence of calcium carbonate (SIC).

steps.title: Fine‑grind subsample for analysis
steps.instruction: Weigh ~10 g of the sample, finely grind it to <53 μm using a Fritsch Mortar Grinder Pulverisette 2 at 50–60 Hz for 4 min.

steps.title: Determine total carbon by combustion
steps.instruction: Measure soil total carbon (STC) using the combustion method: for 2002 samples use the Leco1 CHN analyser; for 2015 samples use the Elementar vario MAX CNS.

steps.title: Determine SOC for 2002 samples
steps.instruction: Treat the 2002 sample with 2 M HCl to remove inorganic carbon, then analyse the residue with the Leco1 CHN analyser to obtain soil organic carbon (SOC).

steps.title: Determine SOC for 2015 samples
steps.instruction: Apply the Walkley‑Black wet oxidation method (using chromic acid) to the 2015 sample and analyse to obtain SOC.

steps.title: Calculate inorganic carbon content
steps.instruction: Compute soil inorganic carbon (SIC) by subtracting SOC from STC (SIC = STC – SOC).
